findings.title: Allah's name orients the refuge appeal
findings.claim: Within 114:0-3, the basmala's designation of Allah is the verbal threshold of the explicit refuge call, with the following titles carrying that appeal toward its human addressee.
findings.mechanism: The focus carriers are the construct-bound name in بِسْمِ and Allah's proper name. In 114:1, قُلْ أَعُوذُ introduces a commanded, voiced refuge appeal; Rabb, Malik, and Ilah of people then continue specifying the one approached across 114:1-3. The designation and proper name therefore meet an ordered refuge act, changing the opening from a static label into the verbal orientation of that appeal.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can perceive the basmala already facing the appeal that begins after it, while still hearing its ordinary naming formula.
findings.containment: The basmala does not itself say 'I seek refuge' or replace its plain 'In the name of Allah' sense. The raised-designation image is etymological and does not claim loudness or formal efficacy.

epistemic.reason: A trusted cross-run support states the threshold relation, while the legacy walk supplies the raised-designation extension; the ordered context is explicit, but the elevation remains an image-level resonance.

findings.title: A raised designation meets concealed speech
findings.claim: Against the later hidden whisper in people's chests, the opening name can carry an elevated-designation image: it stands as a distinct naming register beside the surah's concealed speech.
findings.mechanism: The focus carrier is the noun 'name' in بِسْمِ. Its root image of elevation and the supplied account of a name as a raised designation meet two separate context cues: 114:1 commands قُلْ, an utterance, while 114:4-5 identify hidden whispering and locate it in people's chests. Their contact changes the opening name from an isolated label into an explicitly named speech surface set alongside concealed inward speech.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can notice that the surah first names its orientation and then describes a voice that works inwardly and out of sight.
findings.containment: The designation remains a name in the plain basmala. The contrast does not establish an acoustic volume, a public broadcast, or a good reputation spreading among people; that further claim lacks an independent trigger here.

epistemic.reason: Trusted cross-run support and legacy walks share the name/whisper contrast. The root elevation image is retained as contextual resonance, while the unsupported good-reputation branch is explicitly left out.

findings.title: Mercy reaches the inward site of whispering
findings.claim: The paired mercy epithets can be heard as close, containing care around the inner person whose chest is later named as the site of whispering; kinship and womb images offer qualified analogies for that care.
findings.mechanism: The focus carriers are the two mercy adjectives. The refuge request and Rabb title in 114:1 meet their active compassion/protection sense; the later whisper in the chest (114:4-5) gives that care an inward object, and 114:6 names jinn and people as the whisper's source categories. The root's kinship image and the womb's containing image contact this refuge/chest sequence as analogies, changing the pair from attributes alone into care imagined around a vulnerable interior.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can perceive the opening mercy as responsive to the inward vulnerability the surah later describes, with intimacy and containment as additional images of care.
findings.containment: The plain mercy wording remains intact. The breast is not a womb, the context does not assert a literal family bond or anatomy-based protection, and this image does not guarantee an outcome.

epistemic.reason: The trusted cross-run support itself grades the protective reading weakly, while several legacy walks articulate it. Refuge and chest are explicit context contacts; kinship and womb remain multi-step analogies rather than lexical senses selected by the adjective forms.

findings.title: A named surface and care for the inward person
findings.claim: With the concealed whisper now in view, the basmala's raised designation and mercy terms can be read together as an explicit naming surface coupled with close care for the exposed inward person.
findings.mechanism: The carriers are the name noun and the paired mercy adjectives. The later contrast between commanded saying in 114:1 and hidden whispering in 114:4-5 gives the name's raised-designation image a speech-channel contact; the chest and the hidden jinn/people categories in 114:5-6 give the mercy pair an inward object, while the kinship branch lends an analogy of closeness. Together these separate contacts change the opening formula into a paired image of explicit naming and intimate care.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can see two different responses already present in the opening: a name on the explicit side of speech and mercy directed toward the inner person later placed at risk.
findings.containment: This is a contextual pairing of the ordinary name and mercy terms. It does not claim that the name itself is loud, that mercy literally means family, or that the focus says the later whisper has already been removed.

epistemic.reason: The paired reading is carried by a legacy retrospective walk and combines two multi-step contacts. Its components have separate contextual anchors, but the synthesis remains interpretive.
